issues: Sheets 01-02: the first 2 s are an empty board then a fade-in, and the title and matrix stay static for the first 4 s while the narration says 'rotates any point a quarter turn'; nothing shows rotation.

Sheets 02-12: the whole composition is pinned to the top 20 percent of the frame and the lower 55 percent is dead blank board for 19 s. Nothing uses the vertical frame; the graph only appears at 19.5 s and the caption sits far below.

Sheets 18-25 (11-13): the payoff, the quarter-turn on the plane, arrives only at 19.5 s and the actual turn at 23.7 s; the viewer waits 19 s of algebra before seeing the point move. The graph is small, thin-lined and low contrast, and the labels '(3, 1)' and '(-1, 3)' are tiny and unreadable on a phone.

Sheets 04-09: the worked arithmetic line '0 x 3 + (-1) x 1 = -1' is tiny, thin chalk text under the matrix and nobody can read it on a phone. The result appears at 6.7 s, long before the narration says it at 11 to 12 s, so the visuals run ahead of the voice and the answer is spoiled.

Sheets 06-10: the row highlight is weak (yellow on numbers only), and the full row sum shows instantly rather than building term by term. At sheet 09-10 the highlight stays on the vector after the answer lands, and the result column highlight at 17 to 19 s is not synced with 'three, one lands on'.

Sheets 01-13: the captions are small, change size from frame to frame (the font size jumps between 'This matrix rotates' and 'any point a'), sit far from the action and break into fragments such as 'quarter turn' that don't match the narration phrasing. The caption text also differs from the spoken script ('A matrix turns a point' title versus 'This matrix rotates').
Sheet 02: the annotation 'point three, one' is tiny, yellow on green and overlaps the matrix bracket and an arrow line, and it lingers through sheet 06.

Sheets 12-13: the pink '(-1, 3)' point is the only motion that carries meaning and has no trail or right-angle marker, so the quarter turn is hard to read as 90 degrees. The video ends abruptly on a held frame with the caption 'turn'.
